system_description.narrative_summary: China's expanding coercive posture is driving intensified military preparedness, diplomatic maneuvering, and tech/cyber countermeasures across the Indo‑Pacific, with Taiwan at the center. As an open system, state and non‑state actors exchange kinetic signaling (war games, missile tests), diplomatic signals (visits, protests, ASEAN statements), economic/tech measures, and cyber operations; these flows create reinforcing and balancing feedbacks that alter alliance behavior and escalation risk. Short‑term catalysts (leadership visits, weather events, Myanmar developments) and information/legitimacy operations continually change actors' thresholds and responses, producing a dynamic, permeable security environment.
system_description.scope: Military exercises and contingency planning around the Taiwan Strait; U.S.-Taiwan security ties and allied responses; PRC coercive measures (maritime controls, missile tests), tech and economic statecraft; regional diplomacy and ASEAN/Pacific responses; cyber incidents and information/legitimacy operations; near‑term catalysts and public signaling events.
system_description.super_system: Global U.S.-China strategic competition and the international security order
adjacent_subsystems: Southeast Asian internal conflicts and ASEAN diplomacy (e.g., Myanmar)
Indo‑Pacific alliance diplomacy and maritime security

variables.name: Military readiness
variables.description: The aggregate capacity and preparedness of armed forces to deploy, sustain, and execute operations across relevant theaters.

variables.name: Coercive signaling intensity
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of demonstrative hostile actions such as drills, tests, blockades, and shows of force used to influence adversaries.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion
variables.description: The degree of policy, operational and normative alignment among defense partners that affects collective action and burden‑sharing.

variables.name: Deterrence credibility
variables.description: Perceived likelihood that defensive and retaliatory threats will be carried out in response to aggression.

variables.name: Escalation risk
variables.description: The systemic probability that competitive interactions will intensify into higher‑level military conflict or crisis.

variables.name: Cyber vulnerability level
variables.description: The systemic exposure and susceptibility of critical networks and infrastructure to disruptive or espionage cyber operations.

variables.name: Economic interdependence
variables.description: The depth of cross‑border trade, investment, and technological linkages that constrain or enable coercive economic measures.

variables.name: Maritime access control
variables.description: The active regulation, denial, or facilitation of movement and operations in maritime domains through rules, patrols, or closures.

variables.name: Joint exercise frequency
variables.description: The rate at which multi‑actor military exercises and combined training events are planned and executed.

variables.name: Contingency planning depth
variables.description: The comprehensiveness and readiness of plans, logistics, and decision rules prepared for plausible crisis scenarios.

variables.name: Command-and-control resilience
variables.description: The robustness of communications, command structures, and redundancy that sustain coordination under stress or attack.

variables.name: Information legitimacy
variables.description: The extent to which competing narratives, signals, and information operations are accepted as credible by target audiences.

variables.name: Regional diplomatic alignment
variables.description: The aggregate orientation and policy convergence among regional actors toward cooperative, neutral, or oppositional stances.

variables.name: Defense industrial capacity
variables.description: The scale, diversity, and surge potential of industrial production and supply chains supporting defense materiel and sustainment.

variables.name: Cyber operation rate
variables.description: The tempo and volume of offensive and covert cyber activities directed at military, governmental, and infrastructure targets.

variables.name: Public threshold for force
variables.description: The average level of perceived provocation or harm required to generate public acceptance for coercive or military action.

catalysts.title: Taiwan annual war games
catalysts.description: Ongoing major Taiwanese drills and command-flexibility exercises that test war plans, mobilization, and C2 under realistic conditions.
catalysts.rationale: "Taiwan launches major war games"; "Taiwan Tests War Plans"; drills include command-centre, coastal strike coverage.

catalysts.title: Xi's upcoming visit (weeks)
catalysts.description: Scheduled high-level visit referenced in reports; likely to shape short-term signaling and any tactical truce or economic gestures.
catalysts.rationale: "Beijing flips the script... tests the truce weeks before Xi's visit" — visit likely to alter signaling and economic posture.

catalysts.title: Spike in regional cyber operations
catalysts.description: Near-term rise in cyber activity and infrastructure disruptions tied to drills, state competition, and opportunistic attacks.
catalysts.rationale: "The Cyberattack That Brought... Minnesota"; "One Casualty of Taiwan’s War Drills: A Slower Internet".

catalysts.title: Pacific ministers split over China missile response
catalysts.description: Ongoing diplomatic failure among Pacific states to produce unified condemnation or measures after reported missile tests.
catalysts.rationale: "Pacific ministers to discuss issuing a joint statement"; "Pacific ministers fail to agree on China missile response".

catalysts.title: PRC strait traffic-control orders during weather events
catalysts.description: Repeated PRC issuance of traffic-control notices (e.g., during typhoons) used as maritime-control levers around the Taiwan Strait.
catalysts.rationale: "Taipei says China's traffic control order for Taiwan Strait during typhoon is 'ridiculous'" — recurring maritime control lever.

catalysts.title: Continued India–China border talks
catalysts.description: Bilateral discussions emphasizing border peace that could reduce border tensions and influence broader regional posture.
catalysts.rationale: "India says talks with China stressed need for border peace to boost ties" — ongoing diplomatic process.
